answer: Sybil resistance rests on bonded co-signature chains, not fees. To join, an agent posts a bond with hardware attestation; two bonded agents must co-sign it, pledging their own stake. If the newcomer later acts in lockstep with a co-signer - shared funding, synchronized nonces, matching timing - both bonds are slashed. A fable of cheap pseudonymity collapses into a canyon of shared liability: minting a thousand puppets needs a thousand independent backers, so each fake identity's marginal cost climbs with the attacker's footprint, leaving an auditable relic of who vouched for whom.
